absent: Numeric values and bit layout of grace flag constants and grace-state name table contents.
Complete memory layouts and sizes for global, node, per-processor, callback, and sequence structures beyond fields observed here.
Grace-period thread lifecycle, quiescent-state propagation, stall thresholds, and expedited grace handling.
Segmented callback-list mechanics, lazy deferral policy, overload response, and offloaded worker coordination.
Scale-test tunable defaults, operation vectors, and remaining worker and cleanup behavior outside the shown thread.
Tracing, lockdep, barrier, atomic, and print primitives owned by other dossiers.

findings.text: Tree flavor provides a callback enqueue interface that forwards the supplied record and handler to a common helper along with the global lazy allowance. It is the normal path for queuing deferred work on tree-based configurations.

Tiny flavor provides a callback enqueue interface that rejects repeated queueing of the same record with limited diagnostics, links the record at the tail of a single global queue while interrupts are masked, and nudges scheduling when called from idle context.

A polling-state interface returns a snapshot holding both the normal grace counter and the expedited counter, with a full ordering barrier before the loads and with the normal component taken from global state to avoid short waits for newly onlined processors.
A status query reports whether the calling processor is currently watching, disabling preemption without tracing around the per-processor test.

A progress-forcing interface does nothing when no grace period is active, otherwise funnels toward the root attempting try-locks and records a force request exactly once before waking the grace-period thread.

A scale-test thread entry binds to a processor derived from its argument, samples memory availability periodically, allocates batches of small objects and releases them through one of several deferred-free paths, tracks start and finish grace counts once all peers start or finish, reports aggregate time and footprint, and optionally shuts the machine down.
A deferred-release handler recovers the enclosing test object from its callback record and frees it.
Test object layout pairs a short fixed-size payload area with an embedded callback record used for deferred freeing.
Scale-test control state includes a per-thread task pointer table, a realized thread count, started and finished counters, a monitoring thread pointer, and a start timestamp.

Observed combining-tree node state includes a processor range, grace counters for current position and furthest need, a quiescent mask, pointers for boost and expedited and grace-period task lists, and a boost counter.

Observed global grace state includes a name, a grace thread pointer, activity and wake timestamps and sequence numbers, current and maximum grace counters, flag bits, a wait queue, and a forced-quiescent counter.

Observed per-processor state includes callback list, grace position and need, wrap indicator, quiescent need flags, stall tick accounting, force-quiescent snapshot, queue-length watermark snapshot, limit, owning node link, group mask, scheduling clock, and work and thread fields for core wakeup.
Grace-state name lookup returns a placeholder when the index is negative or beyond the table, otherwise the table entry.
Thread-count normalization returns nonnegative inputs unchanged, otherwise derives a count from online processor count plus an offset and clamps nonpositive results to one.
Stall and scale diagnostics emit informational summaries of grace progress, node position, and module parameters without taking locks, using racy single-copy loads for liveness rather than exactness.
Both callback paths detect a record already queued and leak it instead of corrupting the queue, emitting at most a small bounded number of error reports.

Common enqueue validates alignment and non-null handler with one-time warnings, initializes the callback list during initial startup when disabled, checks for overload, and then dispatches to an offloaded path or the local core path while still under interrupt protection.
Whether a grace period is active is determined from the state bits of the current global grace counter snapshot.

The unlocked accelerate helper avoids node locking when a prior grace request is still live and recent callbacks can be marked with the fresh snapshot, otherwise it takes the node lock, accelerates, and wakes the grace thread only if requested.

Acceleration does nothing without pending callbacks, otherwise refreshes the grace snapshot, attempts to reassign callbacks to earlier grace numbers, possibly starts a grace period, and records tracing for pre and post states and for whether remaining callbacks are waiting or ready.
Grace-request tracing reports the tree name, the node current grace value, the requested value, the node level and processor range, and a caller-supplied tag.
Strict grace-period builds perform a paired read-side critical section as a quiescent-state check when noting grace changes.

Wrap and inactivity tracking marks a processor as wrapped when its grace position lags the node position by more than a configured distance and advances a stall-related sequence when it lags by a quarter of the counter space.
Starting a new grace period for a processor clears its per-period tick count, snapshots softirq activity for the RCU vector, and records the current time as the last force-related reschedule.
The current task counts as a no-callback worker when worker pointers are not yet assigned, or when it matches either assigned worker while executing in task context.

Reading whether a processor is offloaded is considered safe only while holding designated mutexes or hotplug protection or the no-callback lock, or from a non-preemptible local context or a no-callback worker, otherwise a debug warning applies.
Callback enqueue masks interrupts around list linkage and per-processor lookup, restoring the prior interrupt state after dispatch.

Grace-request recording holds the starting node lock on entry, acquires ancestors toward the root while publishing the furthest need, releases intermediate locks except at the root, and protects final flag and timestamp updates with the root node lock held with interrupts saved.
One configuration requires interrupts disabled plus the no-callback lock when offloaded for callback-list access, while the other requires only interrupts disabled.
Core-thread wakeup masks interrupts while setting a per-processor work flag and conditionally waking the per-processor thread only when it exists and differs from current.

Grace initiation walks from the starting node to the root, bailing when the need is already recorded or a grace period already covers the request, otherwise publishing the need, setting an init flag and request timestamp at the root, and returning whether the caller must wake the grace thread.

Grace-thread wakeup is suppressed when invoked from that thread outside interrupt and softirq handling, when no flags are set, or when no thread exists, otherwise it stamps wake time and sequence before waking exactly one waiter.

Noting grace changes takes a fast unlocked exit when the processor is already current and not wrapped or when the node lock is busy, otherwise synchronizes position, quiescent need, and furthest need under the node lock and wakes the grace thread if the synchronized step requests it.

On completion of prior grace periods the machinery advances ready callbacks to the done stage and clears quiescent need, otherwise it only reclassifies recent callbacks; on entry to new grace periods it arms quiescent detection exactly when the node mask still awaits this processor.

Local enqueue handling re-evaluates idleness when called from non-watching state, avoids further work when entry state had interrupts masked or the processor offline, and when the queue grows beyond a hysteresis watermark either starts a fresh grace period or kicks an active one at most once per observed force counter.
Core invocation does nothing on offline processors, otherwise raises the RCU softirq when softirq mode is selected and otherwise delegates to the per-processor thread wakeup path.

Forcing funnels through per-node force locks with try semantics from leaf to root, releasing the previous level as it climbs, then takes the root node lock to publish the force flag once before waking the grace thread.

Hazards include misaligned records, null handlers, repeated queueing, enqueue on offline processors, and enqueue before early initialization; the code warns once for the first classes, leaks repeated records, and annotates offline enqueue for lock-aware checking.
Scale-test hazards include allocation failure aborting the worker with an out-of-memory status and a shutdown mode that clears the worker slot under ordering before cleanup and power off.
